title: Office & Commercial Movers in Tustin | SOS Moving
metaDescription: Commercial movers in Tustin, CA for staged office relocations: crews Monday through Sunday, 8AM to 6PM, a certificate of insurance for your building.
heroSubtitle: Staged office relocations in Orange County, with your building’s paperwork settled before move day

faq.question: Can you move our Tustin office over a weekend?
faq.answer: Yes. Crews work Monday through Sunday inside 8AM – 6PM, so a Saturday or Sunday stage is an ordinary booking rather than a favour. Weekend dates carry the Friday-to-Sunday tier: two movers and a truck at $135 in cash or $145 by card, three at $175 or $185, four at $215 or $225.

faq.question: Will you issue a certificate of insurance our property manager accepts?
faq.answer: Yes, for $50. Send the wording your property manager supplies: at The District at Tustin Legacy, for instance, the certificate has to name a list of additional insureds and Vestar Development Co. as certificate holder. We issue it before move day, and we also ask management for the dock and freight lift arrangements at the same time.

faq.question: How much does an office relocation in Tustin cost?
faq.answer: It is hourly. Two movers and a truck are $119 cash or $129 by card Monday through Thursday, three movers $159 or $169, four movers $199 or $209, with higher Friday-to-Sunday rates. A 3-hour minimum applies, drive time counts double past 10 miles, a job 30+ miles from our base carries a 4-hour minimum, and hours past eight are billed as overtime.

faq.question: Can the move run in stages so we do not lose a working day?
faq.answer: That is the usual shape of the job. Departments or floors move one at a time, so people who have already moved are working while the next group packs. Boxes that cannot be delivered between stages can stay loaded on the truck overnight for $200 instead of being carried twice.

faq.question: Do you run night moves in Tustin?
faq.answer: No. Our working window is 8AM – 6PM, seven days a week, and we would rather say so than promise a night crew we do not staff. If a building only permits loading outside those hours, tell us at the walkthrough and we will be straight with you about whether we fit.

faq.question: Our office sits in Old Town, where the curb is tight. What then?
faq.answer: We plan the truck position with the building or the city rather than hoping for a space. The city points drivers to the three public parking lots in Old Town when the curb beside a business is unavailable, and work inside the public right-of-way requires an encroachment permit from the Engineering Division. A second truck, if one is needed to shorten the carry, is $200.
